subject: Dedicated capacity deep-dive request — OrbitAI (capacity planning)
messages:
From: Samira Khan <samira@orbitai.com>
To: lukas.meyer@redwoodinference.com, marissa.cole@redwoodinference.com
Date: 2027-05-14T08:12:00-07:00
Subject: Dedicated capacity deep-dive request / OrbitAI production profile

Hi Lukas / Marissa,

Thanks for the intro, Vivek. We're ramping OrbitAI's public beta and are evaluating dedicated capacity with Redwood for the next phase. We have a few concrete asks and would love a short deep-dive to align expectations on fleet sizing + what committed resources look like.

Quick summary of what we can share today (see attachment for a 48h sample):
- Peak concurrent sessions: ~1,600 sessions (chat-style websocket sessions) with 95th-percentile concurrency focused in US west region.
- Typical prompt size: 120–250 tokens; average response: 220 tokens. Heavy use of streaming for progressive responses.
- Embeddings: background batch jobs ingesting ~15M documents/month, generating 768-d vectors in batch windows (not latency-sensitive).
- Traffic shape: primary 11:00–14:00 PT and 17:00–19:00 PT weekday spikes; occasional weekend campaigns.

Attached: orbitai-traffic-sample.csv (48h), a small telemetry snippet.

Main asks:
1) High-level GPU footprint to hit 99th-percentile latency target of 300ms for interactive chat p99 token latency (not p99 response end-to-end).
2) Options for autoscaling vs reserved pools for our usage profile and cost tradeoffs.
3) Any recommended quantization/parallelism profiles we should test for the Llama-variant we're evaluating (we'll be testing 13B and 33B).

Can we set a 45-minute call today or tomorrow? Happy to share more logs before the call.

Best,
Samira
Head of Infra, OrbitAI

-- attachment: orbitai-traffic-sample.csv (CSV, 45 KB)
From: lukas.meyer@redwoodinference.com <lukas.meyer@redwoodinference.com>

Cc: marissa.cole@redwoodinference.com, priyom.das@redwoodinference.com, vivek.kulkarni@redwoodinference.com
Date: 2027-05-14T09:02:00-07:00
Subject: Re: Dedicated capacity deep-dive request / OrbitAI production profile

Thanks Samira — this is exactly the kind of detail we need, appreciate the sample. I looped in our pre-sales and solutions engineering leads so we can come prepared.

Quick next steps from our side:
- I'll review the 48h sample and run a quick throughput estimate against both your 13B and 33B model candidates.
- Marissa / Priyom: can you pull two rough configs (conservative + aggressive) we could present in a 30–45m call? Include GPU SKUs, expected token throughput, and lead time for provisioning.
- Samira: if you can share an example conversational prompt (1–3 examples) and confirm streaming behaviour (do you flush partial tokens every 200ms?), that will help our p99 token latency modeling.

Proposed times for a 45m deep-dive: 2027-05-14 10:30 PT or 15:30 PT. Which works for you?

I'll also attach a short capacity template you can fill for any missing fields.

Thanks — Lukas
Director, Solutions — Redwood Inference

From: marissa.cole@redwoodinference.com <marissa.cole@redwoodinference.com>

Cc: priyom.das@redwoodinference.com, aditya.rao@redwoodinference.com
Date: 2027-05-14T09:21:00-07:00
Subject: Re: Dedicated capacity deep-dive request / OrbitAI production profile

Lukas — thank you. A couple of notes for the call so we don't lose time:
- For 13B we usually size conservatively around 32–48 concurrent request slots per A100-80GB when streaming (depends on prompt/response token lengths); for 33B the effective slot count drops (roughly 10–16). We'll validate with Priyom's sim.
- Embeddings workload is a separate cost + provisioning path — recommend a mix of reserved batch nodes (for throughput) and spot for processing windows.
- Ask OrbitAI whether they need isolation (dedicated pools per workload) or if shared pools with tenancy are acceptable. Isolation changes SLA and cost.

Priyom: please prepare a lightweight sim that models token-at-a-time generation with a 200ms flush. If we can get the sample token time distribution, we can produce a more precise GPU count rather than a wide range.

Marissa
Sr. Pre-Sales Engineer, Redwood Inference
From: Jake Turner <jake.turner@orbitai.com>
To: lukas.meyer@redwoodinference.com, marissa.cole@redwoodinference.com
Cc: Samira Khan <samira@orbitai.com>, solutions@orbitai.com
Date: 2027-05-14T11:38:00-07:00
Subject: Re: Dedicated capacity deep-dive request / OrbitAI production profile

Thanks — quick follow-up with clarifications and a couple of numbers from infra:
- Confirm streaming flush: yes, we flush partial tokens every ~150–250ms depending on network conditions; typical is 200ms.
- Token distribution (from sample): median prompt 140 tokens, median response 190 tokens, 95th response 420 tokens.
- Peak RPS: 4,200 requests/sec across the region during peak windows, but these map to 1,600 concurrent websocket sessions; requests are often amortized across sessions as users send multiple short prompts in a session.
- Embeddings pipeline: peak batch parallelism requires ~150 concurrent vectorization workers during nightly windows (can be scheduled).

Also, two asks for the call:
1) If you can, prepare an order-of-magnitude cost delta between reserved-only vs hybrid reserved+autoscale for the conservative footprint.
2) Any constraints or recommendations for our load balancer config (session affinity / routing) to keep p99 token latency predictable.

Attaching orbitai-prod-telemetry-snippet.json for the time window we mentioned.

Best,
Jake
Infra Lead, OrbitAI

Subject: Re: Dedicated capacity deep-dive request / OrbitAI production profile

Great data — thanks for the quick turnaround. We have a 45m slot at 2027-05-14 15:30 PT and will take that; Marissa and Priyom will run the sim live and present two sizing options and a recommended canary plan.

Preliminary notes so you have expectations before the call:
- Ballpark conservative (33B workload): ~8–12 x A100-80GB equivalent for steady-state serving with streaming optimizations; bursts may require temporary burst nodes or queueing to keep p99 token latency under 300ms.
- Ballpark conservative (13B workload): ~3–6 x A100-80GB equivalent. These are coarse until we run the sim against your 95th-tail token sizes.
- Embeddings: recommend a separate reserved batch pool sized for nightly throughput; cost-effective to use larger instances with high IO throughput for the ingest phase.
- Autoscaling: hybrid model recommended — reserved baseline to cover 60–70% of expected steady demand + burst pool that scales on queue depth/CPU. This avoids cold starts for streaming sessions.

Action items:
- Marissa / Priyom: run sim and present GPU count + estimated token throughput in the call.
- Vivek / Lukas: prepare rough cost delta (reserved vs hybrid) post-call for OrbitAI procurement.
- Samira / Jake: if you can drop the three representative prompts into the redwood-capacity-template (we'll use them in the sim), that will speed iteration.

See you on the call.

Cheers,
Lukas
Director, Solutions — Redwood Inference
